title: service-policy-scoped-rbac-and-kms-provenance-mux
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context and motivation: We need a lightweight way to bind RBAC v2 policy scope to service-level configuration and to ensure KMS selection includes provenance signals for residency and operator attestation. Existing region-pin and KMS scoping logic lives in multiple places (ingress, kms allocator, operator proxy). This PR centralizes the enforcement contract:
- annotate ingress routes and service configs with a "service-policy" tag that drives an RBAC v2 evaluation scope
- introduce a KMS provenance multiplexer (provenance_mux) that picks a KMS execution path by combining tenant residency claim, service-policy constraints, and operator attestation tokens
- wire an encrypted, signed audit forwarder to ensure audit events emitted from the mux and RBAC enforcer include a provenance header and are forwarded reliably to the compliance pipeline

What this change includes:
1) RBAC: add service-scope-aware evaluation. The rbac engine understands a new annotation 'service_policy' present on API ingress and service manifest. Policy compiler now accepts evidence: service_policy, tenant_region, callsite_attributes.
2) KMS provenance multiplexer: a thin orchestration layer that chooses between primary-cmk, regional-cmk, and ephemeral-operator-wrapped keys. The mux embeds a provenance attestation blob into KMS requests so downstream auditors can verify why a key was selected.
3) Audit forwarder: audit events from both RBAC decisions and KMS mux are compressed, HMAC-signed, and sent to the audit ingestion topic. A local retry queue and backoff are included to avoid dropping critical provenance events.
4) Integration tests + e2e scenario: new integration harness exercises region-pin failure, operator-claim expiry, and ensures audit envelopes validate.

Checklist:
- [x] Add annotation parsing and service_policy propagation
- [x] Implement provenance_mux decision tree and fallback rules
- [x] Emit signed audit envelopes from mux and rbac enforcer
- [x] Integration tests for residency mismatch and fallback
- [x] Add metrics (rbac.decisions_by_policy, kms_mux.path, audit.forwarder.latency)
- [x] Documentation note (security/ops) in changelog

Files touched: see files_changed list below for specifics.

Backwards compatibility notes: service_policy annotation is optional; if omitted behavior falls back to tenant-scoped RBAC rules. KMS mux introduces a new provenance header but the KMS adapter understands and ignores it when talking to legacy providers.

Rollout strategy: staged rollout behind feature flag 'service_policy_mux' with a shadow-mode for 48h then opt-in enforcement per-namespace.

Risks and mitigation:
- Misconfigured service_policy could widen operator scope: mitigation includes linter rules in CI and a deny-by-default compiler mode.
- Audit forwarder outage: local durable queue and alerting on queue depth, plus short-term retention in blobstore.

merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2025-01-17 by Maya Chen. Commit message used: 'service: bind service_policy to rbac scope; add kms provenance_mux and signed audit forwarder — ENG-9342 SEC-224'. Merge method: squash and merge. Post-merge actions: feature flag enabled in canary namespace, ops runbook added to docs/security/service_policy_mux.md
release_notes: - Add service-level RBAC scoping via 'service_policy' annotation (opt-in behind feature flag). - Introduce KMS provenance multiplexer that selects key execution path and emits provenance headers for auditability. - Audit forwarder now signs and compresses audit envelopes and provides a local retry queue. - Metrics: rbac.decisions_by_policy, kms_mux.path, audit.forwarder.queue_depth. See docs/security/service_policy_mux.md for rollout steps.
additional_notes: Testing notes: integration harness includes a simulated legacy KMS provider that ignores provenance headers; tests confirm backward compatibility. Ops: watch rbac.enforcer.denied_by_policy and audit.forwarder.queue_depth during rollout. Follow-up work tracked in ENG-9401 (policy-linter integration with SDK templates).
